title: Vikas Yadav & Vishal Yadav v. State of UP & Anr. (Nitish Katara Murder Case)
crime_type: Honor Killing / Abduction / Corpse Incineration by Chemical Fuel
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Delhi
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1359141)
ipc_sections: Section 364 IPC (Kidnapping in order to murder)
Section 34 IPC (Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention)
location: Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh & New Delhi, India
evidence: Tata Safari vehicle seen transporting victim from wedding venue in Ghaziabad by key witness Bharat Divakar
Charred human wrist watch and single burnt shoe recovered from roadside furnace in Khurja matching victim apparel
DNA profiling confirming charred unidentifiable skeletal remains matched victim mother Neelam Katara
Hammer and blunt trauma tools recovered from agricultural tube-well shack
modus_operandi: Abducted young corporate executive from a friend wedding party under pretext of private conversation due to disapproval of his romantic relationship with their sister. Drove victim to secluded farmland in Khurja, battered his skull with iron hammers, soaked the body in diesel, and set it ablaze to prevent identification.
personality_disorder: Feudal entitlement, violent misogynistic honor preservation, and sociopathic contempt for law.
common_traits: Brutal blunt force execution based on caste and status honor
Chemical fuel incineration of corpse to thwart post-mortem DNA
Prolonged legal delay tactics leveraging political influence
summary: Supreme Court landmark ruling on honor killings in India. The Court characterized honor killings as rare and cold-blooded acts of barbarity, enhancing sentences to 25 years rigorous imprisonment without remission for Vikas and Vishal Yadav.
